# Can more of the same cell do new jobs?

<!-- STEP id="one-cell" -->
## One cell, every job

An amoeba is a single cell. That one cell takes in food, moves, gets rid of waste and divides to make new amoebae. **In a unicellular organism such as amoeba, a single cell performs all the functions of life.**

<!-- STEP id="you-began" -->
## You began as one cell

Your body also began as a single cell. That cell divided many times and gave a large number of cells. Slowly these cells formed your skin for protection, your muscles for movement, your bones for support and your nerves for control.

<!-- STEP id="same-cell" -->
## A clump of the same cell

Now picture a different path. The first cell divides again and again, but every new cell stays exactly like the first one. The clump grows from a few cells to the size of a rabbit, and every cell still does every job, just as an amoeba does.

<!-- STEP id="question" -->
## The question

A bigger clump has more cells, but does it have any new abilities? **Can more copies of the same cell give a body new kinds of work, or only more of the same work?**

image.alt: A small ball of identical purple cells grows step by step into a clump the size of a rabbit, with labels for problems such as getting nutrients and oxygen inside, removing waste and repairing damage.
